Mesos

Distributed version of a board game · my favourite project

A Java client-server game over TCP sockets and RMI, with both a JavaFX GUI and a text interface. Each of us went deep on two or three parts, then we put them together into the full picture.

Show detailsHide details
  • Built on MVC and the State, Observer, Factory and Proxy patterns.
  • My part: model logic, the text interface, GUI layout in FXML, action handling in the controller, command-line parsing, JUnit unit and integration tests (84% overall coverage), UML diagrams and documentation.
  • Advanced features: a leaderboard stored in MySQL via JDBC, saving and restoring games after a server crash, and handling of player disconnections.
  • Java
  • JavaFX / FXML
  • RMI
  • TCP sockets
  • JUnit
  • MySQL / JDBC
  • UML

Hardware component in VHDL

Priority-ordered task list in external memory

A logic circuit that manages a priority-ordered task list in external memory, with four operations and a handshake protocol, implemented as a 23-state Moore machine.

Show detailsHide details
  • Synthesized on an Artix-7 FPGA with Vivado: 112 LUTs, 71 flip-flops, no inferred latches, and the 20 ns clock constraint met with a wide margin.
  • Verified with behavioural and post-synthesis simulation, plus my own extended 11-step testbench for edge cases the course testbench did not cover.
  • VHDL
  • Xilinx Vivado
  • Artix-7 FPGA
  • FSM design

The Impossible Catering

SAT solver for a scheduling problem

A C solver for a Boolean satisfiability problem: backtracking with unit propagation and a variable-selection heuristic, plus binary search on the number of requests to drop.

Show detailsHide details
  • Large inputs handled with static data structures and binary search on names.
  • Evaluated automatically against test cases, in the style of programming contests.
  • C
  • SAT
  • Backtracking
  • Binary search
